rounds.text: Univastu India Ltd presents a compelling fundamental profile, anchored by explosive top and bottom-line expansion, including a compounded sales growth of 163% and compounded profit growth of 214% over the trailing twelve months [E17, E21]. This hyper-growth is supported by elite capital efficiency, highlighted by a stellar ROCE of 26.6% to 30.0% and an ROE reaching up to 25.4%, both of which vastly outpace respective sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E12, E13]. Valuation remains highly attractive given a moderate P/E ratio of 13.2x and a discounted cash flow intrinsic value estimate of Rs 454 per share, translating into a massive margin of safety of 68.3% [E1, E44, E45]. Furthermore, institutional money flow signals positive accumulation with domestic institutions increasing their stake, while the rules-based screen awards the company a high-confidence BUY score of 98 out of 100 [E42, E43, E64]. Conceded: debtor days have expanded to 121 days alongside a cash conversion ratio of 0.46x indicating profits are running ahead of cash, and promoter holding has declined by over five percentage points [E33, E40, E62].

Univastu India Ltd carries several notable financial risks and deteriorating operational indicators that warrant caution despite headline numbers. Operating margins are eroding, with TTM operating margins slipping to 14% from 16% three years earlier and quarterly margins falling even more sharply to 13% in September 2026 compared to 17% in the year-ago quarter [E29, E30], accompanied by an inconsistent yearly and quarterly margin trend [E31, E32]. Working capital health is under severe strain as debtor days have doubled from 58.4 to 121 days [E62], directly resulting in a poor cash conversion ratio of 0.46x for March 2026 where reported profits far outpace actual operating cash flow [E33]. Furthermore, insiders are quietly reducing their stake, with promoter holding dropping by over five percentage points from 72.87% in December 2023 to 67.46% by September 2026 [E40]. Shareholders also receive zero return on their capital through dividends despite the reporting of repeated profits [E4, E61], while the stock itself carries a high annualised volatility of 50.5% [E53]. Conceded: [E44] (a discounted cash flow puts intrinsic value at Rs 454 per share against a market price of Rs 144, leaving a significant margin of safety).

While the bear points to declining margins [E29, E30, E31, E32], this compression is heavily outweighed by explosive top-line and bottom-line expansion, including a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 163% and profit growth of 214% [E17, E21]. On working capital and cash conversion [E33, E62], the business still generated a positive operating cash flow of Rs 12 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs 11 Cr in March 2026 [E34, E35], while simultaneously reducing its total borrowings to Rs 34 Cr [E38]. Regarding insider ownership [E40], promoters still retain a commanding majority stake of 67.46% [E40], and institutional money flow has actually turned positive with domestic institutions increasing their holding [E42, E43]. Conceded: [E4, E61] (the dividend yield is 0.00% and the company is not paying out dividends despite repeated profits). Finally, the high volatility noted by the bear [E53] is paired with a stellar relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 and a twelve-month price return of 90.6% [E50, E51], supported by an elite rules-based screen score of 98 out of 100 [E64].

Conceded: [E17, E21, E34, E35, E38, E42, E43, E50, E51, E64]. However, citing explosive top-line and bottom-line expansion ignores the severe deterioration in working capital and cash collection, highlighted by debtor days swelling from 58.4 to 121 days [E62]. This massive divergence between reported profits and actual cash realization explains why cash conversion sits at a weak 0.46x, pointing directly to severe receivables and accrual risks [E33]. Furthermore, dismissing margin erosion is dangerous when operating margins have contracted by 2 percentage points in the TTM and by 4 percentage points in the latest quarter, maintaining an inconsistent trend [E29, E30, E31, E32]. While the bull points to a commanding promoter majority, it glosses over the steady insider distribution that has reduced promoter holdings by 5.41 percentage points since December 2023 [E40]. Finally, pairing high annualized volatility of 50.5% with a 0.00% dividend yield despite repeated profits means shareholders bear substantial price risk without receiving any cash returns [E4, E53, E61].
